History and Physical (Detailed)

Consult Summary:
23-year-old woman with 2-day history of constant dull lower-abdominal ache, nausea, and subjective fever; no vomiting; increased urinary frequency without dysuria; light vaginal spotting; GP video visit arranged face-to-face today for examination, pregnancy test, and further work-up.

History:
• Presenting complaint: Constant dull ache below umbilicus for the past 2 days, accompanied by nausea and feeling hot/sweaty.  
• Onset/progression: Gradual over 2 days; worsening discomfort prompting consult.  
• Exacerbating/relieving factors: None identified.  
• Associated symptoms:  
  – Increased urinary frequency (no urgency, dysuria, malodor, or flank pain).  
  – Light pink spotting over last few days; expecting period soon (LMP ≈3 weeks ago).  
  – No vomiting, diarrhoea, or persistent constipation (was constipated one week ago, now resolved; last BM yesterday).  
  – No vaginal discharge, dyspareunia, shoulder pain, syncope, or light-headedness.  
• Pertinent negatives: No urinary pain; no foul-smelling urine; no diarrhoea; no discharge.

Past Medical History:
• No chronic medical conditions reported.  
• Allergy: Amoxicillin (reaction not specified).  
• No prior surgeries or hospitalisations documented.

Medications:
• Etonogestrel implant (Implanon) – dose/route/frequency not documented (long-acting subdermal).  
• No other regular or PRN medications.

Social History:
• Lives with boyfriend.  
• Sexually active with single partner; uses implant contraception.  
• Non-smoker.  
• Alcohol and recreational drug use: not discussed.

Family History:
• Brother with type 1 diabetes.  
• No other familial diseases reported.

Physical Examination:
Not recorded (video consult without exam or vitals).

Investigations:
• None performed during consult.  
• Plan to obtain: urine pregnancy test, urinalysis ± culture, pelvic and abdominal examination; additional tests as guided by findings.

Assessment & Plan:
Overall Impression:
Lower-abdominal pain with systemic symptoms in reproductive-age woman; key concerns are urinary tract infection, early/ectopic pregnancy, and pelvic inflammatory disease. Constipation less likely but possible contributor. Requires in-person assessment today.

DDx Integration:
1. Urinary tract infection (cystitis ± early pyelonephritis) – supports: frequency, suprapubic ache, subjective fever; opposes: no dysuria/urgency, normal-appearing urine.  
2. Early intrauterine or ectopic pregnancy – supports: spotting, pelvic pain, nausea; opposes: effective implant contraception, pain not acute/severe.  
3. Pelvic inflammatory disease – supports: pelvic pain, feverishness, spotting; opposes: no discharge or dyspareunia.

Issue 1 – Acute lower-abdominal pain / pelvic pain:
• Arrange same-day face-to-face GP review for abdominal, pelvic, and bimanual exam.  
• Urine dipstick and culture; serum/urine β-hCG to rule out pregnancy/ectopic.  
• Baseline vitals, FBC, CRP if infection suspected.  
• Safety-net advice given: seek urgent care if pain worsens, develops dizziness, fainting, heavy bleeding, or other concerning symptoms.

Issue 2 – Possible urinary tract infection:
• If urinalysis positive: treat empirically per local guidelines (pending culture) considering amoxicillin allergy; counsel hydration.  
• If negative, re-evaluate DDx.

Issue 3 – Possible early/ectopic pregnancy:
• Urgent pregnancy test today.  
• If positive or equivocal, arrange quantitative β-hCG and early pregnancy/TV ultrasound per protocol.  
• Advise patient on red-flag symptoms (sudden severe pain, shoulder tip pain, syncope).

General plan items:
• Provide information leaflet on pelvic pain and when to seek emergency care.  
• Schedule follow-up after investigations or earlier if symptoms change.

Quality checks:
● Missing elements: No vitals, physical exam, alcohol/substance use history—will obtain at in-person visit.  
● Transcript/DDx conflicts: None noted.  
● Transcript quality: Clear; occasional conversational overlaps but clinically adequate.
